evidence: Wikipedia's article on 'Modern Sounds in Country and Western Music' (recorded February 1962, released March 1962 on ABC-Paramount): the album includes two Hank Williams songs, 'You Win Again' and 'Hey, Good Lookin''. It became one of the best-selling albums by a Black musician of its time and one of the best-selling country albums, and its mix of soul and country is described as challenging racial barriers in popular music at the height of the Civil Rights Movement.

trackPair.whatToListenFor: Williams's version is a fast, bouncing honky-tonk song with fiddle and steel guitar. Charles turns it into big-band swing: horns, a walking bass, and a voice that plays with the rhythm instead of riding on it. Listen for the melody, which barely changes, and for everything around it, which changes completely.

explanation: In 1962 Ray Charles made an album of country songs, including two by Hank Williams. It was one of the best-selling records of the year, at a time when country was seen as white music and soul as Black music: a soul singer taking the songbook of a white country writer, who had himself learned guitar from a Black blues musician, back across the colour line. Wikipedia also notes that in making it Charles became one of the first African-American musicians to have complete artistic control over his own recordings.
